vulnerability_analysis: The Milesinu contract has three fee parameters that can be set by the owner: _taxFee, _DevFee, and _liquidityFee. Each fee is calculated as a percentage of the transfer amount. The vulnerability is that these fees can be set to excessive values (e.g., 30% each, totaling 90%), allowing the owner to extract value from token transfers. When fees are collected, they accumulate in the contract and can be converted to ETH via swapAndLiquify, with half going to DevAddress (which the owner controls) and half adding liquidity where the LP tokens go to the owner.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner. 2. Set all three fee percentages to high values (e.g., 30% each). 3. Enable swapAndLiquify. 4. Transfer tokens to trigger fee collection. 5. The accumulated fees will be swapped to ETH, with half sent to DevAddress (which we control as owner) and half used to add liquidity (LP tokens go to owner).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner. 2. Call setTaxFeePercent(30), setDevFeePercent(30), setLiquidityFeePercent(30). 3. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(true). 4. Optionally set DevAddress to attacker address. 5. Transfer tokens from one address to another to trigger fee collection. 6. Wait for swapAndLiquify to execute (or trigger it manually by meeting conditions). 7. Check that attacker's ETH balance increased.
